entry.title: A shared room can serve different ages
entry.summary: Davies describes shared rooms with places for each child’s belongings and privacy. Older children’s small parts stay truly inaccessible to younger children.
entry.cue: One child reaches for another’s work, or a shared room needs clearer places.
detail: Her storage examples keep older children’s small parts genuinely out of younger children’s reach, or in containers the younger child cannot open. If an activity can be simplified for the younger child, that is a separate way to join.
She also describes places for personal belongings and for being alone, with clear agreements about using a shared space. This is different from sending an upset toddler away.
For small homes, fewer displayed items and useful storage can create room. The purpose is a home that works for its people.

references.locator: Higher shelves actually out of reach or inaccessible containers

references.section: General principles / Sharing and small spaces
references.locator: Unsuited objects out of reach; personal space, simplified participation, agreements and small-space options

ageContext.bookAge: The home discussion covers siblings of different ages; it gives no fixed age for a shared-space arrangement.
ageContext.readiness: Shared belongings, privacy, and younger children reaching older children’s small parts.

displayContext.footer: You don’t need a different home. Start with what you have.
displayContext.colophon: Original summaries inspired by The Montessori Baby and The Montessori Toddler. Open any idea for its book references. The illustration is an invitation to explore, rather than a room to reproduce. Follow your child’s pace.
